novel_mechanics_found: Level 9's decisive mechanics, discovered live this session: (1) A single 7 hunter contacting the 8 converts it to c directly (no e required), with an ~11px knockback away from the attacker. (2) Hunters LATCH adjacent to a fruit after an up-to-12px lunge, and a latched or occluded hostile degrades the fruit one tier on the NEXT transition -- but a pull applied to the fruit in that transition resolves BEFORE the hostile attack, so towing the fruit every single transition fully suppresses degradation. (3) When the fruit being chased is dragged near several converging hunters, they mass-lunge onto it and become fully occluded; from that occluded pile the full four-hunter d composite formed spontaneously (7+7->e twice, e+e->d) without any explicit player-driven hostile choreography -- the c fruit acting as bait consolidated all four hunters into d in a handful of transitions. (4) The d composite is PULLABLE like a fruit (a click within ~8 drags it to the click point). (5) The win fired the moment c (with d riding occluded beneath it) was pulled into socket 1 while f sat in socket 2: delivering the c+d stack into one socket satisfied the level -- no separate d-to-third-socket delivery was needed. (6) ACTION7 undo costs zero resource meter (it only costs an env step and does not refund the undone click), which makes undo-probing of dangerous transitions essentially free against the meter budget. (7) A c->b degrade flips all sockets and the requirement display to color 2 (red), a clear 'requirement now unsatisfiable' signal, and is cleanly reversible by one undo.
narrative: Replayed the 145-action banked prefix from a fresh reset and confirmed level 8 (GameState.NOT_FINISHED, meter full at 64). Opened with the known-good line: click (26,46) merged both 6s into f (1 meter cell), then (20,49) and (14,53) staged f into socket 2's edge, (32,54) kited the 8 away from hunter D, and (11,55) deep-socketed f. During these steps hunter D contacted the 8 and converted it to c with knockback -- no e was needed. All four hunters then converged on the free c. Dead end 1: letting a latched hunter sit adjacent for one neutral transition degraded c->b and flipped the board red; recovered with one free undo. Probing continued: dragging c west to (14,44) caused a mass lunge that occluded all four hunters under c; a neutral transition from that pile degraded c again (dead end 2, undone twice). Dragging c southeast to escape revealed the four hunters had fused into the complete d composite (its spikes showed at c's edge), which then chased and re-occluded under c. A deliberate sacrificial branch (advance one transition, let d degrade c) separated d for a pullability test: a click near d alone dragged it obediently -- d is pullable. Undid the sacrificial branch, then executed the endgame: towed the c+d stack with back-to-back pulls (20,47) then (14,43) toward socket 1, pulling every transition so d's attack never fired. The second tow landed c inside socket 1 with d riding beneath it and the game immediately declared GameState.WIN at levels_completed=9 -- a full game clear, with only 18 of 64 meter cells spent and 164 total actions. A fresh-reset reproduction gate (arc_solver_kit.reproduce) replayed all 164 actions and confirmed reached_level=9.
gotchas: Pull-first ordering is the whole game: a click's drag resolves before hostile attacks in the same transition, so a fruit under active attack is safe as long as EVERY transition includes a pull affecting it; any 'rest' transition while a hostile is latched/occluded loses a tier.

The c+d stack is inseparable by pulls (both are pullable and share a center, so any click catches both), but you never need to separate them: deliver the stack into a socket and the win fires with d riding under c.

Do not fear the mass hunter pile-on: baiting all four hunters onto the kited c is exactly what forms the d composite for free -- the fusion chain resolves inside the occluded pile within a few transitions.
A single 7 (not just an e) converts the 8 into c on contact, with ~11px knockback away from the attacker; position the 8 so the knockback sends c somewhere useful.

ACTION7 undo is free against the resource meter (env-step cost only, no refund of undone clicks), so probe dangerous transitions liberally: act, observe, undo. Deep multi-step undo works (two consecutive undos verified).

Hostiles (7s, d) do NOT trigger the two-different-tier click-interference failure -- only real fruits do; clicks beside a latched hunter or the occluded d succeed at normal 1-2 cell cost. The f no-click zone (~10.5px around the socketed f) remains the main interference hazard on the left side.
Deep-socketing f does NOT strand or repel hunters chasing it; they keep coming, but a socketed fruit is never degraded in practice because the chase retargets to the free c once it exists.

The whole winning continuation from the level-8 state is 19 actions (5 of them free undos): merge 6s at (26,46), stage f via (20,49),(14,53),(11,55), kite the 8 once at (32,54), consolidate hunters onto c, let them fuse to d, then tow the c+d stack via (20,47),(14,43) into socket 1. Meter spent: 18/64 -- the prior round's meter exhaustion was from kiting/failed clicks, not intrinsic level cost.
c->b degrade turns sockets and the requirement display red (color 2): instant, unambiguous 'you just lost a required tier' feedback -- undo immediately, the flip is fully reversible.
